comparison: Perfect agreement on tumor growth acceleration claims (C4, C34-C39). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported through Kaplan-Meier survival, tumor burden measurements, histology, and proliferation markers. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'valuable' and 'convincing.'

Complete agreement on tamoxifen resistance claims (C6, C40-C45). Both evaluations affirm the evidence is strong and systematic. Editor explicitly confirms 'FRMD8 holds potential as a therapeutic target for reversing tamoxifen resistance,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of controlled experiments with appropriate statistical significance.

Full agreement on methylation mechanism claims (C15, C91-C94). Both evaluations support the TCGA analysis and 5-Aza-dC validation experiments. OpenEval notes that direct bisulfite sequencing would strengthen conclusions, but peer reviewers accept findings as part of convincing evidence base without raising this concern.

Partial agreement on prognostic value claims (C16, C95-C97, C118). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes marginal statistical significance (p=0.0409) and need for larger cohorts. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 specifically noting 'Whether FRMD8 can become a biomarker should be verified in large clinical samples,' indicating both identify validation needs.

Strong agreement on post-translational regulation and competitive inhibition mechanism (C11-C14, C77-C88, C121). Both evaluations praise the comprehensive biochemical evidence including co-IP, GST pull-down, mass spectrometry, and ubiquitination assays. Peer Reviewer 1 specifically highlights 'two ways in which FRMD8 affects ERα' as a strength, matching OpenEval's assessment of convergent evidence.

Agreement on transcriptional regulation mechanism via FOXO3A (C9, C66-C71, C120). Both evaluations support the gain/loss of function studies, epistasis analysis, and ChIP-qPCR data. OpenEval notes the mechanism by which FRMD8 regulates FOXO3A levels remains unclear, but peer reviewers describe the mechanistic investigation as 'thorough' without raising this specific concern.

Agreement on luminal phenotype loss claims (C5, C7, C50, C56-C57, C63). Both evaluations support the scRNA-seq and immunofluorescence convergence. OpenEval notes mechanistic link requires further investigation; peer Reviewer 1 highlights single-cell sequencing as a strength. Peer review includes additional claims (C51-C52, C54, C58-C62, C102-C105) related to cell characterization and hormone receptor downregulation.

Agreement on hormone receptor downregulation (C8, C54-C62). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements (~5-fold reduction) across multiple approaches. Peer review groups these claims with luminal phenotype loss findings, treating them as part of the systematic investigation praised by reviewers.

Agreement on post-translational regulation mechanism (C3, C64-C65, C72-C76). OpenEval highlights cycloheximide chase assays and inhibitor experiments as demonstrating lysosomal degradation. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'two ways' FRMD8 affects ERα, though they group these claims with transcriptional regulation findings in their evaluation.

Overlap on post-translational regulation details (C72-C76). OpenEval groups these with broader post-translational mechanism (R6), while peer reviewers include them with competitive inhibition mechanism (R5). Both evaluations support the evidence; difference is organizational rather than substantive disagreement.

Agreement on background/context claims about breast cancer and tamoxifen resistance (C1-C2, C19-C24). Both evaluations accept these as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly affirms the clinical significance of tamoxifen resistance research.

Agreement on literature context claims (C27-C33). Both evaluations accept these prior findings as appropriately cited background. Peer Reviewer 1 notes 'research on the role of FRMD8 in breast cancer is very limited,' implicitly accepting these citations in other contexts.

Agreement on scRNA-seq dataset characterization (C46-C49, C53, C89). Both evaluations support the technical quality and methodology. OpenEval notes CNV-based characterization of normal cells could benefit from additional validation; peer Reviewer 1 specifically praises single-cell sequencing technology as a strength.

Agreement on additional literature context (C101, C106-C108, C110-C111). Both evaluations accept these as supporting background with appropriate citations. No concerns raised about accuracy or relevance of prior work citations.

Divergent evaluation of core conclusions (C17, C98-C100, C119, C122). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, distinguishing well-supported mechanistic findings from speculative therapeutic implications. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with editor confirming FRMD8's potential as therapeutic target. Both acknowledge speculative elements but differ in overall assessment.

Divergent evaluation of therapeutic speculation (C18, C117, C123). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these represent future work rather than demonstrated results despite appropriate qualification. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming FRMD8's potential while acknowledging speculative nature. Difference reflects stricter vs. more permissive standards for forward-looking claims.

Minimal overlap on speculative biological effects (C109, C112). OpenEval includes these in UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting they require additional validation. Peer reviewers accept the 'logical coherence' without specific concerns, grouped with other contextual elements.

Minor overlap on cell characterization details (C51-C52, C102-C103). OpenEval groups with scRNA-seq methodology evaluation, noting CNV-based normal cell characterization could benefit from validation. Peer reviewers include these with luminal phenotype findings without raising validation concerns.

Minor overlap on background statistics (C113-C116). OpenEval groups with established background knowledge. Peer reviewers include with contextual/speculative elements, accepting overall logical framework.
Minimal overlap on background claims (C25-C26). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited literature context supporting the study rationale.
